t: Set up Branchlane with the Git, SSH keys and remotes you already have. Branchlane uses the git that is already on your Mac. If macOS asks to install the command line developer tools the first time, accept it. Branchlane has no account to create. Toolbar. Undo, fetch, pull, push, branch and stash. The number on Push is how many commits you have not sent yet. Left panel. Local and remote branches, pull requests, stashes, tags and Git Flow. ⌘J hides it. Commit graph. Each branch keeps a straight line. The // WIP row at the top is what you have not committed yet. Right panel. Changes, the commit box and the assistant. Click a commit in the graph to see what it changed. ⌘K hides it.

Open a repository. Choose Add Repository ( ⌘O ) and pick a folder, or Clone Repository ( ⇧⌘O ) and paste a URL. Allow your Git identity. The App Sandbox keeps Branchlane out of your home folder until you say so. In Settings > Git & SSH, choose your .gitconfig once so commits use your name and email. Allow SSH keys if you use key files. Keys loaded in ssh-agent already work. To use key files and ~/.ssh/config , choose your .ssh folder in the same place. Sign in to HTTPS remotes when asked. Branchlane asks for a username and token the first time a remote needs one, and keeps it in your Keychain only if you choose to remember it.

These are the same Git and SSH settings the app uses. Skip what you already have. # Command line developer tools and Git xcode-select --install git --version # The name and email that go into your commits git config --global user.name "Alex Kim" git config --global user.email "alex@example.com" # Load your key into ssh-agent and test GitHub ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 ssh -T git@github.com If the last command ends with You've successfully authenticated , your SSH remotes work in Branchlane as they are.
Stage, commit, branch, undo, stash and read history.

The right panel lists unstaged and staged files. Stage a whole file, or open it and stage single hunks or lines. Write a summary and press Commit, or Commit and Push. Files to stage and the commit box. Turn on Amend to change the last commit

Select lines in a diff and Stage Lines and Discard Lines appear below. Use them to commit or throw away part of a hunk. Lines are written to the index byte for byte, so files with CRLF line endings or other encodings stay as they were. Staging only the five lines of a new function
New Branch is ⌘B and Switch Branch is ⇧⌘B . In the graph, drag one branch onto another to merge or rebase it, or right-click a branch for every action. Fetch is ⇧⌘F , Pull ⇧⌘L and Push ⇧⌘K .
A merge commit is named after the branch, as in Merge branch 'develop' into feature . Settings > Git & SSH > Merge can show the full ref ( refs/heads/develop ) or the commit hash instead.
⌘Z takes back checkout, commit, reset, discard, branch delete, stash drop and rebase, and ⇧⌘Z redoes. Undo is kept in Git itself, so it still works after you quit.
Stash Changes is ⌥⌘S and Pop Latest Stash ⇧⌥⌘S . Select a file and press ⇧⌘H for its history, or open blame from a diff.

If you know the command line, this is roughly what each action does. The Git console ( ⇧⌘C ) runs Git commands directly too. In Branchlane Similar Git command Stage a file git add <file> Stage hunks or lines git add -p <file> Unstage All git restore --staged . Amend git commit --amend Commit and Push git commit -m "…" && git push New Branch ⌘B git switch -c <name> Stash / Pop git stash push / git stash pop File history ⇧⌘H git log --follow -- <file>
Interactive rebase, the conflict editor, pull requests and AI. These need Branchlane Pro. Every new eligible subscriber can try them free for 14 days.

Right-click a commit and choose Interactive Rebase. Reorder, reword, squash and drop, then start the rebase. Undo takes the whole rebase back. A plan that folds 12 commits into 8. The result is at the top and the keys are at the bottom Keys are faster in the list: P pick, R reword, S squash, D drop, and ⌥↑ ⌥↓ to move a commit.

When a merge, rebase or cherry-pick stops, open a conflicted file. Both sides sit side by side at the top, and the result is below. Conflict warnings show collisions before you merge. Ours. The branch you have checked out. Theirs. The branch being merged in. Result. Conflicts you have not settled stay red, and parts that merged on their own are marked. Choose for each conflict. Your change, theirs, both, both in reverse order, or the base, or edit it yourself. When all are done, press Continue in the bar at the top.

Choose a provider in Settings > Assistant: a local model, your own API key, or Apple's on-device model. Nothing is sent until you ask. Ask the assistant with ⇧⌘I . Changes it suggests wait on a card until you run them. What it read folds out above, and anything that changes the repository waits on a card To run a model on this Mac, pull one with Ollama and put http://localhost:11434 in Settings > Assistant. ollama pull llama3.2 curl -s http://localhost:11434/v1/models

Worktrees, compare, Git Flow and patches are in the left panel and the right-click menus. Pull requests and issues: add a GitHub or GitLab token in Settings > Integrations. It stays in your Keychain and talks to the host directly. Themes: themes beyond White and Black are Pro. You can preview every theme in Settings > Themes on the free plan.
The keys you use most. All of them are under ⌘/ in the app.

Press ⌘P and type to find branches, commits, files and commands at once. Press ↩ on a row to check it out or open it. Start with a symbol to look for one kind only. Symbol Finds Example > Commands >push @ Branches @feature/ # Commits #tokenizer / Files /NoteStore + Changed files +README ^ Tags ^v1.0 $ Stashes $shorter

Action Keys Command palette ⇧⌘P Quick open: repositories, branches, commits, files ⌘P Add repository / Clone ⌘O / ⇧⌘O Fetch / Pull / Push ⇧⌘F / ⇧⌘L / ⇧⌘K New branch / Switch branch ⌘B / ⇧⌘B Undo / Redo ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z Stash / Pop latest stash ⌥⌘S / ⇧⌥⌘S Left panel / Right panel ⌘J / ⌘K Ask the assistant ⇧⌘I Git console ⇧⌘C Refresh ⌘R All shortcuts ⌘/

Give each coding agent its own branch and folder, and review its work in one place. Agent lanes give Claude Code, Codex or another coding agent a branch and folder of their own, then let you review and integrate the work in one place. Decide. Send it back, accept it into the queue, or integrate it now. Proposal. The agent's summary and claims. Claims without evidence, or with stale evidence, are marked. Evidence. Tests, builds and lint runs the agent recorded. Each counts only for the content it ran on, and files changed since then are listed. Overlapping work. When another lane or the target changes the same lines, you see the line ranges and which side should land first. Files to review. Risky files come first. Leave out a file or a hunk and that part is not integrated.

Open Settings > Agents and connect your agent. Branchlane shows the exact setting for each agent and only listens on this Mac. Start a lane from the Lanes section of the left panel, or let the agent start one with its own tools. When the agent asks for review, open the lane. Take the whole lane, leave out files or single hunks, or send it back with your reasons. Integrated lanes come back out with one commit.

Once it is connected, ask for the work as usual and add a line about lanes. Work in a Branchlane lane. Retry sync with exponential backoff when the server is busy, record the swift test run as evidence, then ask for review.

A lane is an ordinary Git branch and worktree, so Terminal and other Git tools see it too. git worktree list /Users/me/src/app 9b26e1e [main] /Users/me/src/app/.branchlane/lanes/a7f460dc 4c1d2e0 [lane/retry-sync-with-backoff-a7f4] To connect your own tool, see the developer docs .
What to do where the App Sandbox gets in the way.

h: A hook or script says "operation not permitted"
t: macOS quarantines files written by App Store apps, and quarantined programs cannot run. Hooks and scripts that arrive through a clone, pull or checkout in Branchlane need this once in Terminal, and again after Branchlane writes them later: # Is it quarantined? A value means yes xattr -p com.apple.quarantine .git/hooks/pre-commit # Clear the quarantine flag for the whole repository xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /path/to/repo Branchlane shows the command with your path when this blocks a Git operation. Hooks that were already on disk run normally.
Choose your .gitconfig in Settings > Git & SSH, or set a name and email for this repository from its folder: git config user.name "Alex Kim" git config user.email "alex@example.com"

h: SSH asks about a host key
t: The first connection to a host shows its fingerprint. Check it against your host's published fingerprint and trust it. Trusted hosts are listed in Settings > Git & SSH. You can see the fingerprint from Terminal first: ssh-keyscan github.com 2>/dev/null | ssh-keygen -lf - GitHub publishes its fingerprints in the GitHub docs .

h: A worktree outside the repository shows no changes
t: The sandbox needs access to that folder. Choose Allow Access on the worktree row once, and Branchlane remembers it.

h: There is no terminal inside the app
t: The Git console ( ⇧⌘C ) runs Git commands. For anything else, Open in Terminal hands the repository to Terminal.

Where to ask, and what to include. Ask a question or report a problem on the support page . Include your macOS version, your Branchlane version from the Branchlane menu, and what you expected to happen. Leave out repository contents and tokens.
Connect coding agents and your own tools through a local MCP server, and read what Branchlane keeps in the repository. No cloud API, no account.

Connect an agent Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client, in one line. Lane flow The order of calls, from start to review. Tools Arguments and results of every tool. Policy file What agents may do in a repository.

Branchlane has no cloud API. Everything a tool can reach runs on the same Mac, or lives in the repository where any tool can read it. A local MCP server for agents. Coding agents and your own tools start lanes, save checkpoints, record test evidence and ask for review. Connect Plain files and Git refs. A policy file, Agent Trace notes, commit trailers and a summary of every worktree, all readable without Branchlane running. Policy , attribution Your own AI and MCP servers. Point Branchlane at any OpenAI-compatible model server, and let its assistant call your MCP server over HTTP. Extend Branchlane

Turn on connections in Settings > Agents, copy the token, and see whether the server answers. export BRANCHLANE_TOKEN= "the token from Settings" curl -s http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BRANCHLANE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}' \ | jq -r '.result.tools[].name' lane_begin lane_status lane_checkpoint lane_evidence lane_propose lane_request
The lane server needs Branchlane Pro and runs only while Let agents connect is on in Settings > Agents. Branchlane has no URL scheme, App Intents or AppleScript dictionary.
Add the local MCP server to Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client.

Open Settings > Agents, turn on Let agents connect , and copy the line for your agent. It already holds your port and token. Branchlane never writes these files for you. Claude Code Codex Any other MCP client Run once in Terminal, then check that it connected: claude mcp add --transport http branchlane \ http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>" claude mcp list Add to ~/.codex/config.toml : [mcp_servers.branchlane] url = "http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp" http_headers = { Authorization = "Bearer <token>" } Use the Streamable HTTP transport with the endpoint http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp and the header Authorization: Bearer <token> . The port can be changed in Settings. { "mcpServers" : { "branchlane" : { "type" : "http" , "url" : "http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp" , "headers" : { "Authorization" : "Bearer <token>" } } } } Each client shapes its settings file a little differently. Only the address and the header have to match.

Put the token in an environment variable and start a session: export BRANCHLANE_TOKEN= "the token from Settings" curl -s http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BRANCHLANE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize", "params": { "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": { "name": "my-tool", "version": "1.0" } } }' { "jsonrpc" : "2.0" , "id" : 1 , "result" : { "protocolVersion" : "2025-06-18" , "capabilities" : { "tools" : { "listChanged" : false } }, "serverInfo" : { "name" : "branchlane" , "version" : "1" }, "instructions" : "Branchlane coordinates parallel agents in this repository. Start each task with lane_begin and work in the worktree it returns. …" } } Call a tool. path must be a repository you opened in Branchlane. curl -s http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BRANCHLANE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "lane_begin", "arguments": { "path": "/Users/me/src/app", "intent": "Retry sync with backoff when the server is busy", "agent": "my-tool/model-x", "scope": ["Sources/Sy

Every tool returns its result as a JSON string inside a text item: { "jsonrpc" : "2.0" , "id" : 2 , "result" : { "content" : [{ "type" : "text" , "text" : "{
 "branch" : "lane/retry-sync-with-backoff-a7f4",
 "cloned" : [],
 "lane_id" : "a7f460dc", ... }" }], "isError" : false } } Unpacked with jq , it looks like this: curl -s … | jq '.result.content[0].text | fromjson' { "branch" : "lane/retry-sync-with-backoff-a7f4" , "cloned" : [], "lane_id" : "a7f460dc" , "next" : "Work only inside `worktree`. Commit there as you like; Branchlane snapshots uncommitted work too." , "target" : "refs/heads/main" , "worktree" : "/Users/me/src/app/.branchlane/lanes/a7f460dc" } When a tool fails, HTTP is still 200, isError is true , and the text says why.
The order of calls, and what each state means.

lane_begin , then work only inside the returned worktree. Commit there as you like: Branchlane snapshots uncommitted work too. lane_status before you start and before you propose. It tells you which files other agents are touching. lane_checkpoint whenever you like. The checkpoint hook also saves one at the end of every turn. lane_evidence after your last edit, for each test, build or lint run. Keep the returned ids. lane_propose with a summary and claims that cite those ids. lane_status later, for review feedback, left-out files and hunks, and notes.

This shell function calls a tool and unpacks the JSON inside. Use it to do by hand what an agent does, or to try your own tool. lane() { # lane <tool> '<arguments JSON>' curl -s http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BRANCHLANE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"tools/call\",\"params\":{\"name\":\"$1\",\"arguments\":$2}}" \ | jq '.result.content[0].text | fromjson? // .' } lane lane_begin '{"path":"/Users/me/src/app","intent":"Retry sync with backoff","agent":"me/manual"}' cd /Users/me/src/app/.branchlane/lanes/a7f460dc # the worktree it returned # … edit and commit … swift test; lane lane_evidence "{\"path\":\"$PWD\",\"command\":\"swift test\",\"exit_code\":$?}" lane lane_propose "{\"path\":\"$PWD\",\"summary\":\"Retries with backoff\",\"claims\":[{\"text\":\"Tests pass\",\"evidence\":[1]}]}" { "claims_without_current_evidence" : [], "next" : "The person reviews in Branchlane. Call lane_status later for feedback." , "status" : "proposed" }

running proposed accepted integrated Value In the app When running Working lane_begin, or returned by the person proposed Ready for Review lane_propose accepted In Queue The person accepted it; requireEvidence must pass needsUpdate Needs Update The target moved and the work no longer applies. Rebase onto the target and propose again. integrated Integrated Landed on the target in one commit reverted Reverted Taken back out with one commit abandoned Abandoned Cleaned up without integrating
Every MCP tool, its arguments and what it returns. Results below show the JSON inside result.content[0].text , unpacked. Keys arrive in alphabetical order and the indentation may differ.

Every tool takes these. Argument Type Description path required string Your working directory: the repository, or the lane's worktree. lane_id string Can be left out when path is inside the lane's worktree.

Starts a lane: a branch lane/<slug>-<id> and a worktree under .branchlane/lanes/<id> . Work only in that worktree afterwards. Returns lane_id , worktree , branch and target . Argument Type Description intent required string What the person asked for, in one or two sentences. agent string Your tool and model, such as claude-code/claude-opus-5-5 . scope string[] Paths you expect to change. A hint for collision warnings. target string Branch the work should land on. The repository's main branch if left out. clone string[] Ignored folders to copy from the main worktree, such as node_modules or .build . { "branch" : "lane/retry-sync-with-backoff-a7f4" , "cloned" : [ "node_modules" ], "lane_id" : "a7f460dc" , "next" : "Work only inside `worktree`. Commit there as you like; Branchlane snapshots uncommitted work too." , "target" : "refs/heads/main" , "worktree" : "/Users/me/src/app/.branchlane/lanes/a7f460dc" }

Where the lane stands: its status, whether recorded evidence still matches the code, review feedback, files and hunks the person left out, and collisions with other worktrees or the target, with line ranges and which side should go first. { "branch" : "lane/retry-sync-with-backoff-a7f4" , "collisions" : [{ "advice" : "Your lane should land first. Keep your changes on these lines as they are." , "conflict_lines" : [{ "path" : "Sources/Sync/SyncEngine.swift" , "theirs" : [ "41" ], "yours" : [ "40-60" ] }], "conflicts" : [ "Sources/Sync/SyncEngine.swift" ], "integrate_first" : "you" , "same_files" : [ "Sources/Sync/SyncEngine.swift" ], "with" : "/Users/me/src/app/.branchlane/lanes/c19e02b7" }], "evidence" : [{ "command" : "swift test" , "current" : true , "exit_code" : 0 , "id" : 1 }], "intent" : "Retry sync with backoff when the server is busy" , "lane_id" : "a7f460dc" , "status" : "running" , "target" : "refs/heads/main" , "worktree" : "/Users/me/src/app/.branchlane/lanes/a7f460dc" } After a review it can also carry review_feedback (why it came back), rejected_files (files left out, with reasons), left_out_hunks and note . When the content changes after a run, current turns false an

Snapshots the worktree, uncommitted changes included, without staging or committing. Argument Type Description note string A word about the snapshot. { "checkpoint" : "5f0c8e1…" , "tree" : "b41d9a2…" }

Records that a command ran on the current content and how it ended. It is valid only while the content stays exactly the same, so call it after your last edit. Returns evidence_id . Argument Type Description command required string The command that ran, such as swift test . exit_code required integer How it ended. 0 is a pass. output string The command's output. Only the end is kept, with secrets masked. { "evidence_id" : 1 , "note" : "Valid only while the content stays exactly as it is now. Cite this id in lane_propose claims." , "tree" : "b41d9a2…" }

Asks the person to review the lane as it is now. Claims without current evidence are flagged. Argument Type Description summary required string What changed and why, for the reviewer. claims object[] Statements with the evidence ids that back them: { text, evidence[] } .

{ "name" : "lane_propose" , "arguments" : { "path" : "/Users/me/src/app/.branchlane/lanes/a7f460dc" , "summary" : "Pushes are retried with exponential backoff and jitter. Six attempts at most." , "claims" : [ { "text" : "A busy server is tried again, up to six times" , "evidence" : [ 1 ] }, { "text" : "The library file format is unchanged" } ] }} { "claims_without_current_evidence" : [ "The library file format is unchanged" ], "next" : "The person reviews in Branchlane. Call lane_status later for feedback." , "status" : "proposed" }

Asks to push, force-push or rewrite history. The policy decides, and some requests wait up to two minutes for the person. An approved push runs with the person's credentials. Argument Type Description action required enum push , force_push or rewrite_history . reason string Why, shown to the person. One of three answers comes back, depending on the policy and the person. Denied and declined answers have isError set to true . Approved Denied by policy Declined by the person { "decision" : "approved" , "done" : true , "output" : "To github.com:me/app.git\n 9b26e1e..4c1d2e0 lane/retry-sync-with-backoff-a7f4 -> lane/retry-sync-with-backoff-a7f4" } Rewriting history happens inside the lane branch, by the agent itself. That answer has "done": false and a note saying it may go ahead. { "decision" : "denied" , "reason" : "The repository's policy forbids force_push." } { "decision" : "declined" , "reason" : "The person did not approve it." }
Address, transport, limits, authentication and MCP versions.

Address IPv4 loopback only, 127.0.0.1 . Nothing listens on other interfaces or on ::1 . Default port 47120. Transport HTTP/1.1, one request per connection. Only POST /mcp is served; other methods get 405. There is no SSE stream, so every answer comes back on the POST. Notifications get 202 with an empty body. Body Send Content-Length . Chunked bodies get 411. Bodies up to 4 MiB, headers up to 64 KiB. Auth Authorization: Bearer <token> , a 64-character hex token kept in the Keychain. New Token in Settings replaces it. Missing or wrong tokens get 401. Origin A request with an Origin header that is not localhost , 127.0.0.1 or ::1 gets 403, so web pages cannot call the server. MCP Protocol versions 2025-06-18 , 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 . Methods initialize , ping , tools/list and tools/call , and JSON-RPC batches. Tools only: no resources or prompts. Repositories The sandboxed app can only open repositories the person has opened in Branchlane. Otherwise the tool answers with an error that says so.

Code When 200 A result, also when a tool reports an error ( isError ) 202 A notification, with an empty body 401 A missing or wrong token 403 An Origin that is not this Mac 405 A method other than POST 411 A chunked body, or no Content-Length

Without a token you get a 401. curl -i -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp -d '{}' HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized WWW-Authenticate: Bearer … Unauthorized Several requests can go in one JSON-RPC batch, and the answers come back as an array. curl -s http://127.0.0.1:47120/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BRANCHLANE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}, {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}]' \ | jq '.[].id'

Save a checkpoint at the end of every agent turn. POST /hook/checkpoint takes the hook JSON that Claude Code sends and reads its cwd . If that folder is inside a lane worktree, Branchlane saves a checkpoint and answers {"checkpoint":true} ; anywhere else it answers false and does nothing. Merge this into .claude/settings.local.json : { "hooks" : { "Stop" : [{ "hooks" : [{ "type" : "command" , "command" : "curl -s -m 5 -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- http://127.0.0.1:47120/hook/checkpoint >/dev/null 2>&1 || true" }] }] } } The command fails quietly when Branchlane is not running, so the agent is never blocked.

Send just a cwd , the way Claude Code does. Inside a lane worktree the answer is true . echo '{"cwd":"/Users/me/src/app/.branchlane/lanes/a7f460dc"}' \ | curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:47120/hook/checkpoint \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $BRANCHLANE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @- {"checkpoint":true}
What agents may do in a repository, in one committed file.

.branchlane/policy.json in the main worktree tells Branchlane, and the agents it serves, what is allowed. Commit it so the whole team shares it. Settings > Agents can create it with these defaults: { "forbid" : [ "force_push" , "rewrite_history" ], "protectedBranches" : [ "main" , "master" ], "protectedPaths" : [], "requireApproval" : [ "push" ], "requireEvidence" : [], "sensitivePaths" : [] }

Actions are push , force_push , rewrite_history and integrate . Decision order: a forbidden action is denied. On a protected branch, force-push and rewrite are denied and the rest go to the person. Otherwise actions in requireApproval go to the person and the rest are allowed. requireEvidence lists command prefixes, such as swift test , that must have passed on exactly the proposed content before a lane can be accepted. protectedPaths need an explicit yes for each file in review. sensitivePaths are shown first, on top of built-in ones such as migrations, auth code, CI workflows, lock files and .env files. Patterns follow .gitignore rules. Keys are camelCase. A file that does not parse falls back to the defaults and the error shows in Settings.

Protect release branches too, approve billing code file by file, and accept a lane only with test and lint evidence. { "forbid" : [ "force_push" , "rewrite_history" ], "protectedBranches" : [ "main" , "release/*" ], "protectedPaths" : [ "Sources/Billing/" ], "requireApproval" : [ "push" ], "requireEvidence" : [ "swift test" , "swiftlint" ], "sensitivePaths" : [ "Package.resolved" , "fastlane/" ] } With this policy, an agent that asks for a force push with lane_request is refused at once, without asking the person. { "decision" : "denied" , "reason" : "The repository's policy forbids force_push." }
Settings > Agents also turns the policy into Claude Code permissions.deny rules, so Claude Code itself refuses what the policy forbids.
Commit trailers, Agent Trace notes and lane records. Branchlane marks agent work in the graph and blame for everyone, Free included. Your tool can feed it in three ways.

An Agent: trailer wins. Otherwise Branchlane looks at Co-authored-by: , then at the author and committer, for known agent identities such as noreply@anthropic.com , Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, Devin, Jules and aider. Integration commits that Branchlane makes carry: Lane: a7f460dc Change-Id: I3c1f… Agent: claude-code/claude-opus-5-5

Line-level records live as git notes on refs/notes/agent-trace , one note per commit, in the Agent Trace format (version 0.1.0, application/vnd.agent-trace.record+json ). A note may hold one record, an array, or one per line. Records from other tools on the same commit are kept. Blame shows the lines AI wrote. { "version" : "0.1.0" , "id" : "…" , "timestamp" : "2026-11-23T02:09:00.000Z" , "vcs" : { "type" : "git" , "revision" : "<commit>" }, "tool" : { "name" : "claude-code" }, "files" : [{ "path" : "Sources/Sync/RetryingSyncEngine.swift" , "conversations" : [{ "contributor" : { "type" : "ai" , "model_id" : "claude-opus-5-5" }, "ranges" : [{ "start_line" : 12 , "end_line" : 48 }] }] }], "metadata" : { "com.bbdyno.branchlane" : { "written_by" : "Branchlane" , "lane" : "a7f460dc" } } } Notes travel with refs/notes/agent-trace:refs/notes/agent-trace when you share lanes.

Lanes are stored as Git refs under refs/branchlane/lanes/<id>/ ( state , checkpoints , proposal ). The state commits hold a lane.json . Teammates' lanes are fetched to refs/branchlane/shared/<remote>/<id>/ . Treat these as read-only.

# The Agent trailer of each commit git log --format = '%h %(trailers:key=Agent,valueonly,separator=%x2C) %s' -10 # Fetch the Agent Trace notes from the remote and read one git fetch origin refs/notes/agent-trace:refs/notes/agent-trace git notes --ref =agent-trace show HEAD | jq '.files[].path' # Lane records git for-each-ref refs/branchlane/lanes --format = '%(refname)' git show refs/branchlane/lanes/a7f460dc/state:lane.json | jq '{intent, status}' 4c1d2e0 claude-code/claude-opus-5-5 Retry sync with backoff when the server is busy 9b26e1e Trim blank lines on export

One JSON file that describes every worktree. When a repository has more than one worktree and the person has Pro, Branchlane keeps <git common dir>/branchlane/worktrees.json up to date, at least once a minute. Agents that do not speak MCP can read it instead of running git status in every worktree. It is removed when only one worktree is left. { "version" : 1 , "about" : "…" , "generatedAt" : "2026-11-23T02:09:00Z" , "target" : "refs/heads/main" , "worktrees" : [ { "path" : "…" , "branch" : "lane/retry-sync-a7f4" , "head" : "…" , "access" : "readable" , "uncommittedFiles" : [ "Sources/Sync/SyncEngine.swift" ], "lastChange" : "…" } ], "collisions" : [ { "between" : [ "…" , "…" ], "conflicts" : false , "sameFiles" : [ "Sources/Sync/SyncEngine.swift" ], "conflictLines" : { "Sources/Sync/SyncEngine.swift" : [[ "40-60" , "41" ]] } } ] }

The file sits in Git's common directory, so the same path works from any worktree. f= "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/branchlane/worktrees.json" # Uncommitted files in each worktree jq -r '.worktrees[] | "\(.branch)\t\(.uncommittedFiles | length)"' "$f" # Only the pairs that will really conflict jq '.collisions[] | select(.conflicts)' "$f"
Bring your own model server, or an MCP server for the assistant.

Settings > Assistant accepts any OpenAI-compatible server. Branchlane calls POST ../..//chat/completions with stream: true and reads server-sent events or a plain JSON reply, and uses GET ../..//models to test the connection. Without a path it adds /v1 , so Ollama ( http://localhost:11434 ) and LM Studio ( http://localhost:1234 ) work as they are. A key is never sent over plain HTTP to another machine. # Ollama: pull a model and check that it is listed ollama pull llama3.2 curl -s http://localhost:11434/v1/models | jq -r '.data[].id' # LM Studio: start the server and check the same way lms server start curl -s http://localhost:1234/v1/models | jq -r '.data[].id' When the list shows up, put that address in Settings > Assistant and pick the model. Repository data is wrapped between random BEGIN data-… and END data-… markers, and the model is told that what is inside is data, not instructions.

h: Your own MCP server for the assistant
t: The assistant can call tools on MCP servers that the person adds in Settings > Assistant. Serve the Streamable HTTP transport (protocol 2025-06-18 ) over HTTPS, or over HTTP on localhost. Branchlane sends MCP-Protocol-Version , keeps Mcp-Session-Id , and can add a Bearer token. Stdio servers cannot be started from the App Sandbox.
